frequency_question: What proportion of emergency domestic complex missile manufacturing setups are completed within 35 calendar days from program greenlight?
membership_rule: Includes any documented historical state-level program to domesticate precision-guided cruise missile or high-end aerospace production during an active conflict where technology transfer is accelerated. Excludes basic small arms or non-guided munitions.

cases.name: US wartime transfer of B-29 manufacturing to Soviet Tupolev Tu-4
Emergency domestic establishment of guided missile repair/assembly hubs in Ukraine (e.g., Neptune/Hrim adaptations)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 3 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: Exhaustive for major comparable high-tech missile domestication attempts under emergency wartime constraints.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral transfers between modern states (e.g., Iran/Russia or Western/Ukraine) lack public timeline transparency, but baseline physics of aerospace manufacturing apply.
skeleton: Zero historical examples exist of establishing a high-technology cruise missile manufacturing and assembly line from scratch or via foreign transfer within a 35-day window, given the physical lead times for specialized cleanrooms, CNC milling, guidance system calibration, and rocket motor casting.
multiplier: 0 historical instances out of 3 relevant major wartime high-tech transfer programs achieved operational status in under 35 days (typical physical buildout time is 18 to 36 months).
validity_reason: Physical manufacturing constraints and supply chain lead times for aerospace components remain bounded by industrial physics.
